Rashi on Eruvin 9b:10:1.english: When the walls of the small [courtyard] enter the large one - and protrude into the large one by two or three cubits, because those projections (gippufei) that extend from the large one and stand behind the breach of the small one appear as though they are not from the same wall, which is the case here:

Rashi on Eruvin 9b:11:1.english: And let it say "joined," and it would be permitted - That is: if it appears from the outside, it would be effective, as if the entrance-ends of the walls of the small courtyard, abutting the long walls of the large one, were like this: (*) In the case of the courtyard, its entrances would be wall-ends (gifufei) appearing from the outside, since one would think the large courtyard is only slightly wider than the small one, less than three tefachim on this side and less than three on that side. Now there is no gap of three tefachim between the entrances and the long walls of the large courtyard, and it is like joined:

Rashi on Eruvin 9b:12:1.english: And if you would say that they differ - The inward recesses of the walls from the long side of the large [courtyard].

Rashi on Eruvin 9b:12:2.english: Much - More than three [handbreadths], the large one being much wider than the small one.

Rashi on Eruvin 9b:12:3.hebrew: קטנה בעשר וגדולה בי"א - שאין גדולה עודפת על הקטנה אלא אמה אחת, הרי שלשה טפחים לכאן ושלשה טפחים לכאן, ועובי כניסות הכתלים ממעטין את השלשה מכל צד, דאיכא לבוד:
Rashi on Eruvin 9b:12:3.english: The small one is ten and the large one is eleven - That the large one does not exceed the small one except by one amah, which is three handbreadths on this side and three handbreadths on that side. The thickness of the wall-entrances subtracts the three [handbreadths] from each side, since there is *lavud* (the walls are considered joined).

Rashi on Eruvin 9b:13:1.hebrew: במופלגין מכותל זה בשנים ומזה בארבע - שלא היתה קטנה מכוונת כנגד אמצעיתה של גדולה, אלא משוכה שני טפחים לצד אחד, ויש מהאמה עודפת שני טפחים לכאן וארבעה לכאן, והכניסות דקות, ונשאר מצד אחד יותר משלשה ריוח:
Rashi on Eruvin 9b:13:1.english: Separated from this wall by two and from that wall by four - Which means the small wall is not aligned with the middle of the large one, but is set two tefachim off to one side. Of the amah [of six tefachim], two tefachim are left over on one side and four on the other, the openings are narrow, and more than three tefachim of space remain on one side:

Rashi on Eruvin 9b:1:1.hebrew: רב אשי אמר - לעולם בין לחיים לר' יוחנן מותר, והאי דאמר רבי יוחנן דשייכא פלוגתייהו דרבן שמעון ורבנן להכא, כגון דהוה משך רציפה זו ד' אמות באורך המבוי:
Rashi on Eruvin 9b:1:1.english: Rav Ashi said - Always, it is permitted both according to the cheek-posts [view] and according to R' Yochanan. As for what R' Yochanan said, that the dispute of Rabban Shimon and the Rabbis applies here, [it refers to] a case where this beam (rezifah) was drawn out four cubits along the length of the alleyway (mavoy):

Rashi on Eruvin 9b:2:1.hebrew: לרבן שמעון - יש לבוד בפחות מד' והוה ליה חד לחי, ואמרינן לעיל (עירובין ד' ה.) ד' אמות נידון משום מבוי ויצא מתורת לחי:
Rashi on Eruvin 9b:2:1.english: According to Rabban Shimon - There is lavud (joining) when the gap is less than four amot, and it counts as one jamb (lechi). And we said above (Eruvin 5a) that a gap of four amot is judged as an alleyway, and it leaves the category of a jamb.

Rashi on Eruvin 9b:2:2.english: And another lechi is needed to permit it - This alleyway lies between two lechayim, but from the inner lechi onward, one may nevertheless carry in the alleyway, since to them the inner lechi clearly appears as a lechi, its thickness is deemed a lechi for them, and the alleyway is thereby permitted. So I have heard. But it seems to me that even from the inner lechi onward it is not permitted, for according to R. Yochanan, the inner lechi and inward does not permit at all. But according to the Rabbis, each one stands on its own, and the alleyway is permitted by the first lechi.

Rashi on Eruvin 9b:3:1.english: And as for Rabban Shimon - Granted, even if it is all one structure and is judged as the alley's wall, how could R' Yochanan have learned from Rabban Shimon that he requires a second lechi to permit it? Let this alley be permitted when [the wall is] visible from outside and flush from inside, for presumably, if we establish the first lechi, one pulled it slightly outward toward the exterior (1): For this is the way of all who set up lechayim, so that it is seen from inside and outside that a lechi was established there as a lechi. For if one does not extend the width of the lechi a bit beyond the alley walls, but keeps it even with them, like this (2): it appears as though it adds to the thickness of the alley wall. From outside it is not recognizable as a lechi; only from inside is it recognizable that it is not one of the walls, because its tip is visible from inside. And since the first one protrudes partly outward, when the second came and made it flush from inside with these lechayim, forming a continuous line, and made it a wall nonetheless, let the alley be permitted by that first protrusion visible from outside, for we say below that [a wall] visible from outside and flush from inside is judged as a lechi.

Rashi on Eruvin 9b:4:1.hebrew: מידי הוא טעמא - כלומר מי מותבינן האי תיובתא אלא לרבי יוחנן, דיליף מלבוד דרבן שמעון פסולא להאי מבוי:
Rashi on Eruvin 9b:4:1.english: Is that the reason? - I.e., do we raise this refutation against anyone other than R' Yochanan, who derives from the principle of lavud that Rabban Shimon disqualifies this alleyway?

Rashi on Eruvin 9b:4:2.english: Is not judged - Therefore, if we say lavud (contiguity) applies, he needs another jamb.

Rashi on Eruvin 9b:5:1.english: It was stated: we read (the text) as follows:

Rashi on Eruvin 9b:5:2.english: It appears from within and is even from without - That he set the lechi (a projecting jamb) with its broad side along the length of the alleyway, and did not extend its width slightly outward. Rather, he made its outer edge even with the thickness of the alleyway's walls, so it looks like an addition to the width of the walls and does not appear from the outside to be a lechi. But its inner edge is visible from within, since its thickness projects into the width of the alleyway, like this:

Rashi on Eruvin 9b:5:3.hebrew: נראה מבחוץ ושוה מבפנים - שמשך כל הלחי לחוץ, וחודו הפנימי נכנס בכותלי המבוי, ואינו נראה מבפנים אלא דומה כמוסיף על אורך הכותל, אבל מבחוץ ניכר שאינו מכותל המבוי, שהרי נמשך להלאה מרוחב הכותל: (*):(*)
Rashi on Eruvin 9b:5:3.english: It appears from outside and is level from inside - [The cheek] extends entirely outward, and its inner tip enters into the walls of the alley, so that it is not visible from inside; rather, it looks like an extension of the length of the wall. But from outside it is clear that it is not part of the alley's wall, since it extends beyond the width of the wall. (*):(*)

Rashi on Eruvin 9b:6:1.english: A wall one of whose sides is recessed relative to its other part - That is, the structure steps inward and reduces the wall's thickness at that point, so that the remaining part now projects out from it like a pillar, called a “pilier” [in French].

Rashi on Eruvin 9b:6:2.english: Between - That its entrance appears on the inside and is the same on the outside, like this (*):(*) That the wall is sunken behind it, and the indentation appears on the inside.

Rashi on Eruvin 9b:6:3.english: Whether it appears from the outside and is even on the inside - for example, where the wall is recessed in front of it, so that the opening is not visible to those standing inside, but only to those in the public domain, like this: (*):(*)

Rashi on Eruvin 9b:7:1.english: And Rabbi Yochanan - who explicitly stated above that [such a case] is not judged [under this principle]:

Rashi on Eruvin 9b:7:2.english: Did he not hear this? - [This is] the mishna of R. Chiya, and nevertheless he did not hold it [applicable] here. Here too, how can one conclude from it that it is R. Chiya who said "nidon"? Perhaps he [R. Yochanan] also heard it and did not hold it.

Rashi on Eruvin 9b:9:1.hebrew: חצר קטנה שנפרצה לגדולה קטנה נמי תשתרי - דלא ליסרו בני גדולה עלייהו, אלא ליהוי נמי פתחא לגבה, להיות כשני חצירות ופתח ביניהם, ואע"ג דשוה מבפנים, שהעומד בתוכה רואה כל כתלי אורכה שוין, שאין שם מכותל רחבה לפיאותיה כלום, והוי מלואה. הרי מבחוץ בתוך הגדולה נראין לה שיורין, וכותל זה מכאן ומכאן, אותו עודף שהגדולה עודפת על הקטנה, דהא גדולה בהו משתריא, משום דלדידה נראית מבפנים:
Rashi on Eruvin 9b:9:1.english: A small courtyard that was breached into a large one, the small one too is permitted - The point is not that the residents of the large courtyard impose their restriction on it, but rather that it should have an opening to the large one, so that they are like two courtyards with an opening between them. Although the walls are equal from the inside, in that one standing within it sees all of its walls along their length as equal, since there is no wall of width on its sides at all, and it is full. From the outside, within the large courtyard, remnants appear to it, and this wall on either side is the excess by which the large one exceeds the small one, for the large one is permitted because of them, since to it they appear as the inside.

Tosafot on Eruvin 9b:3:1.english: And according to Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, it must appear as seen from outside and be level from inside - Rashi explains that presumably the first lechi was pulled slightly outward, since it is the way of all who set up a lechi to pull it somewhat outward, so that it is visible from outside and from inside that a lechi was established there. But it is more reasonable to explain that they pulled it slightly inward, for the entire passage implies that [Rava] needed to permit [the alleyway] up to the outer edge of the lechi. How could he have permitted it if they had pulled it outward, which would be into the public domain? How could he permit the public domain, when the walls of a standard alleyway are of equal length?

Tosafot on Eruvin 9b:6:1.hebrew: כותל שצדו אחד כנוס משל חבירו בין שנראה כו' - כאן פ"ה ששקע הכותל מלפניו; ולעיל פירש נראה מבחוץ, שמשך כל הלחי לחוץ, וחודו הפנימי נכנס בעובי הכותל ואינו נראה מבפנים אלא מבחוץ. ונראה דלכך שינה, דלעיל איירי בלחי שמעמידין אצל כותל ודרך להעמידו לצד פנים, ומייתי לה נמי אמבוי שרצפו בלחיים, דהיינו לצד פנים. אבל הכא מיירי בכותל שצידו אחד כנוס משל חבירו, ודרך לעשות בנין כענין זה כשיש שני מבואות זה אצל זה או בית וחצר אצל המבוי, שפעמים מאריכין כותל שאצלו יותר מכותל המבוי. ומה שפירש כאן ניחא טפי, דלפי' הקונטרס לעיל קשה: דאי חשיב נראה מבחוץ כשהלחי לצד הפנימי, היכי משני לקמן בנכנסין כותלי קטנה לגדולה? אכתי נראה מבחוץ הוא, דגיפופי גדולה נראין שהן עובי כותלי קטנה, ומה שנכנס לתוך הגדולה הוי כלחי שפירש הקונטרס. ואין לומר בנכנסין ארבע אמות שיוצאין מתורת לחי, דאין זה שייך בחצר. ומיהו, אי הוי דווקא הא דאמר לקמן בעשר ושני טפחים סגי, אתי שפיר, דמיירי כשאין בעוביו טפח. וריצב"א מיישב בנכנסין כותלי קטנה לגדולה, מיירי שיש היכר איזו הם כותלי קטנה, כגון שכותלי קטנה הולכים בשיפוע ממזרח למערב כמו שעושין לכתלים בראשיהן, וכותלי גדולה שיפועם מצפון לדרום:
Tosafot on Eruvin 9b:6:1.english: A wall one of whose sides is set back relative to its fellow's, whether it is seen, etc. - Here Rashi explains [a case] where the wall is recessed in front of it. And above, [Rashi] explained [it as a case of a wall] seen from outside, in which the whole pilaster (lehi) is drawn outward, its inner edge entering into the thickness of the wall, so that it is not visible from inside but only from outside. And it seems that this is why [Rashi] changed [his explanation]: the above [passage] deals with a pilaster placed beside a wall, which one customarily places on the inner side; and [the Gemara] also cites an alley whose [walls] are fitted with pilasters, namely on the inner side. But here it deals with a wall one of whose sides is set back relative to its fellow's, and it is customary to build in this manner when there are two alleys next to one another, or a house and a courtyard next to an alley, since sometimes they extend the wall adjacent to it beyond the wall of the alley. And what [Rashi] explains here is more acceptable, for Rashi's explanation above is difficult. For if [a pilaster] is considered seen from outside when the pilaster is on the inner side, how would [the Gemara] answer below regarding small walls entering large ones? It is still seen from outside, for the projecting edges (gifufei) of the large [wall] appear to be the thickness of the small walls, and what enters into the large [wall] is like a pilaster, as Rashi explained. And one cannot say that in the case of [walls] entering four cubits, [the protrusion] leaves the status of a pilaster, for that does not apply in a courtyard. However, if [the rule] were specifically what is said below, that ten [cubits] and two handbreadths suffice, it would work out well, since it deals with [a wall] whose thickness is not a handbreadth. And Ritzba resolves [the matter] of small walls entering large ones by saying that it deals with a case where there is a distinguishing mark as to which are the small walls: for instance, the small walls run on a slope from east to west, as is done for walls at their ends, and the large walls slope from north to south.

Tosafot on Eruvin 9b:8:1.hebrew: אי לא סבר לה למה ליה למתנייה - אע"ג דבפ' יוצא דופן (נדה ד' מו:) אשכחן רבי יוסי דתני ברייתא דסדר עולם, ולא סבר לה; יש לומר דהיינו דברי הראשונים ממנו, אבל דברי דבר פלוגתא לא תני:
Tosafot on Eruvin 9b:8:1.english: If he did not hold it, why did he need to teach it? - Although in Perek Yotzei Dofen (Nidda 46b) we find that R. Yosei taught a baraita of Seder Olam and did not hold it, one can say that these were the views of the earlier authorities before him, but he did not teach disputed matters.
